Senior Notes In May 2025, the Company issued Euro-denominated fixed-rate senior notes in a public offering in an aggregate principal amount of € 3.5 billion ($ 3.9 billion), with maturities ranging between 3 and 19 years. The 2028 Notes, 2033 Notes, 2037 Notes and 2044 Notes have interest rates of 2.25 %, 3.125 %, 3.50 % and 3.875 %, respectively. Interest on these notes is payable annually on May 15 of each year, commencing May 15, 2026. The net aggregate proceeds, after deducting discounts and debt issuance costs, were approximately € 3.5 billion ($ 3.9 billion). The Company intends to use the net proceeds for general corporate purposes, which may include, among other things, the refinancing of existing indebtedness. The Company’s outstanding senior notes are senior unsecured obligations of the Company, ranking equally and ratably among themselves and with the Company’s existing and future unsecured and unsubordinated debt. passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: This management’s discussion and analysis provides a review of the results of operations, financial condition and liquidity and capital resources of Visa Inc. and its subsidiaries (Visa, we, us, our or the Company) on a historical basis and outlines the factors that have affected recent earnings, as well as those factors that may affect future earnings. The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and related notes included in Item 8 of this report. This section of the report generally discusses fiscal 2025 compared to fiscal 2024. Discussions of fiscal 2024 compared to fiscal 2023 that are not included in this report can be found in “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in Part II, Item 7 in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2024, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Overview Visa is a global payments technology company that facilitates secure, reliable and efficient global commerce and money movement. We provide transaction processing services (primarily authorization, clearing and settlement) among consumers, issuing and acquiring financial institutions and sellers. We are focused on extending, enhancing and investing in our proprietary advanced transaction processing network, VisaNet, to offer a single connection point for facilitating money movement to multiple endpoints through various form factors and innovative technologies across more than 200 countries and territories. Visa is not a financial institution. We do not issue cards, extend credit or set rates and fees for account holders of Visa products. Financial overview. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Regulatory Risks We are subject to complex and evolving global regulations that could harm our business and financial results. As a global payments technology company, we are subject to complex and evolving regulations that govern our operations. Such regulations may increase in quantity, complexity and scope in response to heightened geopolitical tensions. See Item 1 — Government Regulation for more information on the most significant areas of regulation that affect our business. The impact of these regulations on us, our clients, and other third parties could limit our ability to enforce our payments system rules; require us to adopt new rules or change existing rules; affect our existing contractual arrangements; and increase our compliance costs. As discussed in more detail below, we may face differing rules and regulations in matters like interchange reimbursement rates, preferred routing, domestic processing and localization requirements, currency conversion, point-of-sale transaction rules and practices, privacy, data use and protection, licensing requirements and associated product technology. As a result, the Visa operating rules and our other contractual commitments may differ from country to country, state to state, or product to product. Complying with these and other regulations increases our costs and operational complexity, and reduces our revenue opportunities. If widely varying regulations come into existence worldwide, we may have difficulty rapidly adjusting our products, services, fees and other important aspects of our business to comply with the regulations. Our compliance programs and policies are designed to support our compliance with a wide array of regulations and laws, such as regulations regarding anti-money laundering, anti-corruption, competition, money transfer services, privacy and sanctions, and we continually adjust our compliance programs as regulations evolve. However, we cannot guarantee that our practices will be deemed compliant by all applicable regulatory authorities. In the event our controls should fail or we are found to be out of compliance for other reasons, we could be subject to monetary damages, civil and criminal penalties, litigation, investigations and proceedings, and damage to our global brands and reputation. Increased scrutiny and regulation of the global payments industry, including with respect to interchange reimbursement fees, merchant discount rates, operating rules, risk management protocols and other related practices, could harm our business. Regulators around the world have been establishing or increasing their authority to regulate various aspects of the payments industry. See Item 1—Government Regulation for more information . In the U.S. and many other jurisdictions, we have historically set default IRFs. Even though we generally do not receive any revenue related to IRFs in a payment transaction (in the context of credit and debit transactions, those fees are paid by the acquirers to the issuers; the reverse is true for certain transactions like ATM transactions), IRFs are a factor on which we compete with other payments providers and are therefore an important determinant

credit_strengths.text: Visa's operating margin sits above the sector median, reflecting the toll-road economics of VisaNet, where incremental processed transactions and cross-border volume flow through at high contribution. Revenue growth outpaced the prior year on volume and cross-border activity, though higher client incentives partly offset the gain.

Interest coverage is far above the sector median and improved year over year, with operating income dwarfing gross interest expense. The debt stack is almost entirely fixed-rate senior unsecured notes with long-dated maturities, so refinancing risk is concentrated in the near-term maturity rather than spread across the curve.

key_risks.text: Gross leverage rose year over year and now sits at the sector median, driven by the Euro-denominated issuance that lifted total debt. Net leverage remains modest and below the next risk-band boundary, but the upward direction of gross borrowings warrants monitoring as the new notes season.

A large slug of senior notes matures within the next twelve months, and the company has flagged refinancing of existing indebtedness among the uses of the new Euro proceeds. Execution risk on that refinancing, plus currency exposure from Euro-denominated notes, is a concrete structural consideration.

Regulatory risk is the dominant disclosed exposure: interchange reimbursement fees, routing, localization and privacy rules could raise compliance costs and compress revenue opportunities. Widely varying regimes across markets would make rapid product and pricing adjustment difficult, pressuring the high-margin base.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure and dividends, and free cash flow covers buybacks, but total shareholder distributions slightly exceed free cash flow. The shortfall is bridged from the balance sheet, so distributions absorb essentially all internally generated cash after capex.

Free cash flow to debt is strong in absolute terms though it eased year over year as borrowings grew, and cash flow to debt remains well above the downgrade threshold. Liquidity is adequate rather than ample, with the current ratio only marginally above one and below the prior year.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, anchored by net leverage well inside the lowest band and cash flow coverage with substantial headroom to the next threshold. Profitability exceeds the sector median and the Altman zone is safe, supporting a strong investment-grade-like credit posture.

Our forward view is that leverage stays contained while buybacks remain the swing factor: distributions already exceed free cash flow, so any step-up in repurchases or a litigation-driven expense spike would erode the cushion. Refinancing the near-term maturity is manageable given cash and market access.

credit_strengths.text: Visa 的營業利潤率高於行業中位數，反映 VisaNet 的收費公路式經濟模式：增量處理交易及跨境交易量以高貢獻率流經。收入增長受交易量及跨境活動帶動而超越上年，惟較高的客戶激勵部分抵銷了增幅。
利息覆蓋率遠高於行業中位數，並按年改善，經營收入遠超總利息支出。債務結構幾乎全為固定利率的高級無抵押票據，到期日長，故再融資風險集中於近期到期部分，而非分散於整條曲線。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿按年上升，現處於行業中位數，由歐元計價發行推高總債務所致。淨槓桿仍屬溫和，低於下一個風險區間邊界，但總借款的上升方向值得在新票據逐步成熟期間監察。
一大部分高級票據將於未來十二個月內到期，而公司已將現有債務再融資列為新歐元所得款項的用途之一。該再融資的執行風險，加上歐元計價票據的貨幣風險，是具體的結構性考量。
監管風險是披露的主要風險敞口：交換費補償費、路由、本地化及私隱規則可能提高合規成本並壓縮收入機會。各市場制度差異甚大，將使產品及定價難以快速調整，對高利潤率基礎構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 經營現金流穩健覆蓋資本開支及股息，自由現金流覆蓋回購，但股東分派總額略超自由現金流。缺口由資產負債表填補，故分派基本上吸收了資本開支後的全部內部產生現金。
自由現金流對債務比率絕對值強勁，惟隨借款增加而按年放緩，現金流對債務比率仍遠高於降級門檻。流動性屬足夠而非充裕，流動比率僅略高於一，且低於上年。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為極低，錨定於淨槓桿遠低於最低區間，以及現金流覆蓋率對下一門檻有大幅緩衝。盈利能力高於行業中位數，Altman 區域為安全，支持強勁的類投資級信用狀況。
我們的前瞻觀點是槓桿維持受控，而回購仍是關鍵變數：分派已超自由現金流，故回購任何加碼或訴訟驅動的費用急升將侵蝕緩衝。鑑於現金及市場准入，近期到期的再融資屬可管理。
